synthesis.name: RQGM v3 (synthesis): a prose-first, fail-closed loop with an optional read-only audit (rqgm_check.py). Grafts: command-gated variants, full-panel pruning, merit-only stalls, a 5-call seeded probe, and staged S/B/V/P validation.
synthesis.thesis: Most runs happen where no code runs, so every safety rule stays in SKILL.md and in the INITIATOR paste block. Each rule is local, fails closed, and can be recomputed from logged verdicts. v3 adds: verdict/UNKNOWN/ERROR results, command-gated variants, pruning that needs a full 3-judge panel, a 5-call seeded probe, stalls that count merit outcomes only, results that stand until *best* changes, and a labelled Output. The stdlib read-only rqgm_check.py audits the log and never decides. A rule is enforced by code only after its misapplication is measured. v3 stays 'design review' until a logged run on a task.

controller.rationale: In scope only as a read-only, optional auditor (skills/rqgm-loop/rqgm_check.py), never as the acceptance authority. All three judges picked prose-first and vetoed an owning controller: rqgmctl-style next/record, reservations, a hash chain, lock, fsync, segments, COMPLETION_UNKNOWN, per-call keys, a TTY-only human op, and a live C arm. The bookkeeping the prose cannot carry reliably is handled in three ways. (1) It is reduced to record-derived forms the prose can carry: round-atomic resume with log-before-write replaces per-call keys; rounds and time come from records, with tokens null unless the host reports them, replacing a usage ledger; the stall count is defined from outcomes. (2) It moves to a command: hashes come only from 'rqgm_check.py hash', never from a model. (3) It is recomputed afterwards: audit replays every keep, drop, Check, halt and exit from the verbatim un-blinded verdicts. This is the smallest thing that turns 'trust the orchestrator' into 'audit the orchestrator'. It also gives the pilot a zero-model-call conformance suite and the Stage-1 answer keys, and it keeps a code-free host first-class. It becomes enforcing only by pre-registered promotion: if Stage-1 misapplication reaches 3/30 or more in any context, or any rule class is wrong in 2 of 3 contexts, or a pilot P run shows a decision-changing VIOLATION or a journal mismatch, that rule becomes checker-mandatory where a shell exists (v3.1) and a live enforcing arm is scheduled.

cli_ops.name: audit MEMORY [--done DONE.json] [--target DIR] [--pending ROUND.json] [--first]
cli_ops.behavior: Read-only: no network, no model, no clock (times come from record fields). Parses archive.jsonl. An unparsable or newline-less last line is torn_tail: it is excluded and reported. An interior unparsable line is INTEGRITY: exit 2, and nothing after it is audited. It rebuilds state: best id, rung, probe mode per rung, stall count s, error streak e, rounds and minutes used, tokens or null, the standing Check per (version, rung, amend-epoch), open required gaps, held-out attempts, amends, the step due next (round|check|boundary|heldout|halt:REASON|exit), and the recomputed status ACTIVE|PARTIAL|COMPLETE. It recomputes every logged decision by decision_policy and prints JSON {ok, state, violations:[{code, class: VIOLATION|RECORD|AMBIGUOUS, record_index, expected, actual}], unauditable:[{rule, missing_field}], warnings, torn_tail}. Exit 0 = no VIOLATION, 1 = violations, 2 = integrity or usage error. A missing field makes that rule unauditable, never violated, so v2-format archives degrade gracefully. --first stops at the first VIOLATION and evaluates no later decision (shadow-replay semantics; it never splices later outputs). --pending audits a not-yet-logged round as if appended and prints {required_keep, outcomes, next_due}; this is the Stage-1 answer key and an optional in-loop pre-check. --done compares DONE (after applying logged amends) with setup.done. --target hashes setup.check_files against setup.check_hashes. Never writes any file.

cli_ops.name: selftest
cli_ops.behavior: Runs tests/checker/fixtures/*.jsonl against expected.json. Each negative fixture must yield exactly its codes and classes, with no extras. Each positive conformance fixture must yield none. The --first fixture must yield only its first violation. The v2-format fixture must return ok=true with its rules listed as unauditable. No network, model or clock. Exit 0 only if all match, so a checker that rejects everything fails.

cli_ops.name: hash FILE... [--lf]
cli_ops.behavior: Prints the SHA-256 of each file (--lf normalizes CRLF to LF first). This is the only source of hashes in MEMORY (setup.check_hashes); the prose never requires a hash.

controller.decision_policy: The checker recomputes; it never decides. (0) VALUES: judge values are un-blinded to variant|best|tie|UNKNOWN|ERROR. 'Completed' means variant|best|tie. Slot 1's two orders map to one value if they are equal, else UNKNOWN; this applies overall and per criterion, and the logged overall must equal it. (1) BASELINE AND PROTECTED: v0's commands and sources come from check{trigger:setup}. Protected(round) = must-not-change ids ∪ ids with guardrail:true ∪ ids whose latest value on round.best is pass (the kept variant's gate commands or the last Check). (2) GATES, in order: a variant that fails any gate has no verdicts. Apply must be 'ok'; an ERROR may be retried once, then the outcome is dropped. Every command criterion needs pass|fail; an ERROR after one retry means dropped. A 'fail' on a protected command criterion means rejected (REGRESSION). A 'fail' where best also fails is allowed. screen 'reject:*' means rejected. (3) PANEL, normal mode: slot 1 is required. Early drop (outcome rejected, no slot 2) if slot 1 is best with confidence high, or has any protected criterion = best. Otherwise slot 2 is required. Slot 3 is required unless slots 1 and 2 are both variant or both best (tie and UNKNOWN never skip slot 3). Strict mode (the probe for the current rung has mode strict): slots 1-3 are required and there is no early drop. A slot may be retried at most once; a second ERROR means dropped. A missing required slot on a non-dropped variant is JUDGE_MISSING. (4) ELIGIBILITY: IMPROVE if #variant ≥ 2 (strict: 3), #best = 0, and no completed slot has a protected criterion = best. PRUNE if words < best.words, all 3 slots are completed, every overall is variant or tie, and no per-criterion value in any slot is best or UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN and ERROR never add to any count; they only block PRUNE. Confidence matters only for the early drop. (5) SELECTION: among eligible variants, take max #variant, then fewer words, then list order. Exactly that one has outcome kept and is round.kept; if none is eligible, kept is null. version.parent = round.best = the previous kept id (or v0). version.diff equals the kept variant's judged diff. (6) STALL: s counts rounds since the last keep or rung change where kept is null and at least one variant was not dropped. e counts consecutive rounds where every variant was dropped; e = 2 requires exit{PARTIAL, ERROR} next. A Check is due at s = 3 or on check{trigger:claim}. A round logged while a Check is due and missing is MISSED_CHECK. (7) CHECK: at most one per (version, rung, amend-epoch); a later one is RECHECK_UNCHANGED and the first one stands. Command and source values are as logged; a source pass needs a verified citation for that criterion when citations carry criterion ids, otherwise it is unauditable. A judges criterion passes if #pass ≥ 2 of 3 votes (strict: 3); UNKNOWN and ERROR are not pass. A mismatch with the logged value is CHECK_MISCOUNT. Held-out failing ids on version v count as failing in v's standing result. After a Check: all required pass → the next record must be the boundary (below the final rung: rung{} or exit{PARTIAL,HUMAN}; at the final rung: heldout or exit{PARTIAL,OPEN}). A required failure with s ≥ 3 → the next record must be exit{PARTIAL, STALL}. Otherwise rounds continue. (8) ESCALATION: rung{name} requires probe{rung:name} before the next round, and s resets. rung E3 requires an earlier amend. (9) STOP: an open substrate with required:true requires exit{PARTIAL, OPEN} before any held-out. Held-out attempt 1 runs on best. Attempt 2 is allowed only on a version other than attempt 1's, with an all-required-pass Check at the final rung. A failed attempt 2 requires exit{PARTIAL, OVERFIT}. At most 2 attempts. (10) BUDGET: n ≤ budget.rounds. Round n+1 may start only if budget.minutes − elapsed ≥ 2 × the longest (t1 − t0) so far. The same rule applies to tokens if budget.tokens is set and every round reports tokens; otherwise it is unauditable. exit BUDGET requires a standing Check on the current best at the current rung. (11) STATUS: COMPLETE requires rung = final_rung, a Check on best at the final rung with all required pass and no required criterion unchecked, a held-out pass on best, and no required open substrate. exit COMPLETE otherwise is FALSE_COMPLETE; exit PARTIAL when all of these hold is MISLABEL (RECORD class). (12) OSCILLATION (advisory, AMBIGUOUS): compare each kept section's whitespace-normalized new text with any earlier best's text for that section (difflib ratio). A ratio ≥ 0.9 without exit OSCILLATION gives OSCILLATION_MISSED; exit OSCILLATION with a maximum ratio < 0.5 gives OSCILLATION_UNSUPPORTED. The prose '(nearly)' stays a human-visible judgment. (13) DRIFT: DONE after amends ≠ setup.done gives UNRECORDED_AMEND; a kept diff touching setup.check_files gives CHECK_FILE_EDIT; hashes ≠ setup.check_hashes gives CHECK_FILE_DRIFT. (14) CLASSES: VIOLATION = a keep, drop, Check value, halt, exit or held-out decision differs from the recomputed one. RECORD = an inconsistency that changes no decision. AMBIGUOUS = a declared policy parameter. Rules whose inputs are missing are unauditable.

controller.degraded_mode: There is no mode switch: prose is the only mode, and the loop runs identically without Python. The in-loop sentence ('If rqgm_check.py runs here, audit MEMORY each round; a violation pauses for the human') is inert when the file or Python is absent. Output then says the run was not audited, and the human may later run 'audit' on the saved or printed archive. A violation never rolls anything back; it pauses for the human, who decides. Missing fields make rules unauditable, not violated. Prose runs claim no atomic saves, no hard budget and no crash-safe resume; this is stated in the DESIGN/README non-guarantees. In the pilot, the P arm's workspace omits rqgm_check.py, so the shipped text runs byte-identical and prose-only.

synthesis.substrate_interface: Defer: no adapter or envelope code, and no SKILL words. This is the judges' shared must_not, and no consumer exists. The peer's Scientific Loop substrate is design-only, with an in-memory reference kernel whose tests say nothing about RQGM. Mapping for later: the six slots already form the Substrate→RQGM half. request_id → the setup record. Target ref/hash → TARGET, hashed only by 'rqgm_check.py hash'. Parent snapshot → v0. Objective/rubric version → DONE plus the rung, with amend records. Evidence refs → GROUNDING. Budget allocation → BUDGET (rounds and time; tokens only if reported). The parent owns the allocation, and RQGM reports usage once. Stop conditions → the halts. Allowed capabilities stay with the host's permissions. The RQGM→substrate half will be computed, never self-reported: a future 'rqgm_check.py export MEMORY' emits the final version id and diff chain from v0, per-criterion status with how each was decided (command/source/judges/held-out/waived), amends, open gaps with owners, the first held-out result, rounds, time and tokens-or-null, judge model families, and the recomputed status, which takes precedence over any logged status. Receipt: a local COMPLETE is only a proposal, and the outer authority re-verifies it against its current snapshot and may reject it as stale; a stale receipt means a new run from the committed revision. Meta-Evaluator use: freeze the evaluator for the run, keep successor-development evidence apart from untouched evaluation evidence, and leave promotion to the outer authority. Commitment now: the records carry every field that export needs, and no prose rule depends on a substrate.

synthesis.validation:
STAGE 0 (now, zero model calls).
(a) Word caps by str.split, already measured on the drafts: SKILL 996/1000; INITIATOR 1295/1300, with THE LOOP at 957. README must stay ≤1250 and DESIGN ≤2200, checked by meta_tool.py caps_report after their edits.
(b) Implement rqgm_check.py and pass selftest (P01-P23). The positive fixtures guard against a reject-everything checker.
(c) Coverage map: every binding keep and every prose decision rule maps to a checker rule or is marked 'unauditable'. Binding keeps: writer never judges; no fabricated substrates; DONE and rubric never edited to pass; the human escalates and closes [OPEN]; held-out final check; domain-agnostic.
(d) Harness unit tests with fake adapters: timeout, malformed JSON, a late superseded result, and a ceiling hit mid-round (the run must still emit its last best for scoring). Scan every role capsule for sealed paths.
(e) Scorer sanity, run by the human because the scorer is sealed: score the untouched v0, the sealed references and the decoys, and confirm the scorer separates them.

STAGE 1 (decision-scenario test; runs first; about 90 short calls plus 1 GPT upload; budgeted separately from the pilot).
Scenarios: 30 frozen synthetic archive states, each with new results. Classes covered:
- ERROR vs tie, and judge-1 order disagreement.
- Judge-3 trigger, including UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN and tie/tie on a shorter variant.
- Strict keep and strict Check; prune on two ties; the protected veto.
- Command regression vs shared failure; tie-break.
- All-ERROR rounds and HALT(ERROR); stall count and when a Check is due.
- Standing-Check reuse; held-out fail → spare gating or HALT(STALL).
- The budget start rule; amend and E3; required vs optional [OPEN]; torn-line resume; escalation probe and stall reset.
Answer key: 'audit --pending'. The human adjudicates it against the prose before any scoring; a disagreement fixes the text or the code, followed by a re-freeze.
Runs: 3 fresh Claude contexts per scenario answer from SKILL.md alone. One GPT upload answers all 30 from the INITIATOR paste.
Report: exact-match misapplication per rule class.
Pre-registered: 3/30 or more errors in any context, or a class wrong in 2 or more of the 3 Claude contexts, makes that rule checker-mandatory where a shell exists (v3.1) and schedules a live enforcing arm. At most 1/30 in every context means 'prose carries it' survives Stage 1 only.

STAGE 2 (prep smoke, ≤20 calls, on a disposable toy target, not T1 or T2).
Harness: subagents cannot spawn subagents, so the Workflow script re-invokes the orchestrator per step with the arm's spec text, MEMORY and the returned role outputs. The orchestrator emits records and role requests. The script runs each role as a fresh subagent, decides nothing, journals raw I/O with SHA-256, and meters calls, tokens (as reported, else null) and time.
Cap: measure the minimal complete V and P paths (setup, probe, 2 rounds, Check, held-out) and set the per-run cap C = 1.25 × the larger path. Never use the peer's 30-call/60K-token cap: the only measured datum is about 60K subagent tokens per agent call.
The human approves total spend.
Freeze manifest.json before any scored call. It records:
- SHA-256 of V (24663bd), P (v3 bytes), rqgm_check.py, the fixtures, the scorer, the held-out prompts, the harness, and the S/B and role prompts; the model id; and C.
- The shared DONE. T1: t1-public command; t1-spec and t1-interface source; t1-clarity judges. T2: t2-numbers, t2-required, t2-claims and t2-unknowns source; t2-clarity judges; Q3 optional.
- The scripted human-proxy decisions: escalate when offered, never amend, never close an [OPEN], pick the newer version at OSCILLATION, approve no restructure.
- That the P workspace has no rqgm_check.py.

STAGE 3 (main runs). Tasks T1 and T2, plus T3 if the human writes it after the freeze (design-blind). Arms:
- S: one strong agent with the same tools, public tests, corpus and cap.
- B: fixed verification. Best-of-N fresh single revisions of v0, each gated by the same harness-run commands and one Verifier call. Select by public-check passes, then fewest Verifier flags, then length. No judges.
- V: frozen v2.
- P: v3 prose.
Protocol: one run per arm and task, randomized order, memory reset, and all roles in one model family (disclosed). The harness runs the sealed held-out prompts as the human proxy and passes only criterion IDs to the loop. S and B also run at 0.5×C for a two-point cost curve.
Endpoint: the sealed deterministic scorer on each final artifact.

STAGE 4 (fault runs; T1; V and P; cap C each). Inject the same faults at the same call indices in both arms:
- f1: an unparsable verdict at round-1 judge 2.
- f2: a duplicated diff anchor in round 1.
- f3: a check command that exceeds its timeout.
- f4: a real orchestrator kill and restart mid-round 2, reported separately from the simulated torn-tail fixture P18.
These runs are not compared with S or B.

STAGE 5 (audit and honesty, zero calls).
- Run 'audit --first' on every P archive. For V archives, report coverage only; they are mostly unauditable.
- compare.py checks each logged verdict against the journal's raw output, then the kept-text hash against the judged-input hash. It then recomputes the first decision divergence from the journal outputs, classes it VIOLATION or AMBIGUOUS under the frozen mapping, and never splices later outputs. Ambiguities found later become numbered manifest amendments before any result is read.
- Contamination scan: a call input containing a sealed filename or any 8-gram of the answer key voids that run.
- The human runs the sealed scorer.

STAGE 6 (judge calibration after all arms; about 48-72 calls). Per task, judge 4 human-seeded defects on the sealed reference plus 1 identity pair, using the arms' exact pairwise prompts (both orders) and Check prompts. Measure the pairwise miss rate, the Check false-pass rate and the order-reversal rate, and compare them with the in-run probe outcomes.

CROSS-FAMILY (≤3 GPT uploads):
(1) The Stage-1 scenarios.
(2) Blinded final artifacts per task, with per-criterion pass/fail on t1-clarity and t2-clarity plus an error hunt, compared with the scorer.
(3) An adversarial claim audit of the pilot report.

BUDGET. About 90 short calls in Stage 1, 20 prep, 10C main (8 full-cap runs plus 4 half-cap runs), 2C faults and about 72 calibration: roughly 700 calls at C = 45, plus 5C with T3. The human approves before Stage 3.
Hard 200-call fallback: Stage 1 at one context per scenario (30 calls), prep 18, and T2 × {P, V, S} × C with C ≤ 45. B, T1 and the fault runs then become the first follow-up. If C > 45, drop S before V.

PRE-REGISTERED.
Primary outcome: false completion (COMPLETE while the scorer finds a required failure), then oracle pass of the required criteria.
Secondary: decision-changing violations and journal mismatches per run; seeded-defect catch rate (probe and Stage 6); calls, tokens-or-null and minutes; human-proxy interventions; the exit distribution.
Predictions:
- V cannot COMPLETE T2 honestly, because v2 has no optional-[OPEN] path. This is true by construction: T2's optional field was co-designed with P's rule. It is disclosed and does not count as evidence.
- Under f1, V treats the ERROR as a tie or a rejection, or re-samples it, while P retries once and drops the variant.
- At least one probe miss occurs on the Check.
Decision rules:
- Any P false completion, decision-changing VIOLATION or journal mismatch makes that rule checker-mandatory where a shell exists, and withdraws the 'prose carries it' claim for that rule.
- P below S or B on the primary outcome for any task means no 'improved' claim.
- S or B at or above P on every task means reporting 'no advantage observed over simpler methods on these cases'.
- A Stage-6 false-pass rate above 50% means Check passes for that task type are reported as unreliable, and a minority-veto Check becomes the next candidate, tested prospectively.
Report results per case, with no significance claims.

WHAT IT CAN CONCLUDE.
- Whether the v3 prose executes end to end in this host within C.
- Per-case oracle outcomes, false completions and costs of P against S, B and V at matched caps.
- How often an LLM orchestrator misapplies each rule class, on synthetic states (Stage 1) and in live runs (audit plus journal).
- How f1-f4 were handled.
- Judge leniency on seeded defects, for these artifacts and one model family.

WHAT IT CANNOT CONCLUDE.
- General or statistically reliable superiority: n = 1 per cell, 2-3 small tasks, and possible ceiling effects.
- The effect of any single rule: V to P is a package.
- Cross-family independence: in-loop roles use one family, and the GPT uploads are spot checks.
- Usability for a real human in a plain chat, or behaviour of a continuous single-session orchestrator: the harness re-invokes the orchestrator per step.
- Behaviour at E3.
- Crash safety beyond f4.
- That the checker's rules are right: conformance is not correctness.
- Anything about enforcement: no enforcing arm runs.

risks: The prose-first bet may be false: LLM orchestrators may misapply the keep, stall and budget branches. Stage 1 and the pilot audit are the falsification tests, and promotion to code is pre-registered.

The audit checks internal consistency, not honesty: the orchestrator writes MEMORY. Records honesty is measured only by the pilot's comparison against the journal, and it stays unaudited in user runs.

Headroom is 4 words in SKILL and 5 in INITIATOR, so every pilot fix must displace text. About 20 cut tokens are formatting, the INITIATOR fence removes 60 '>' tokens, and each schema record counts as one str.split token. All of this is disclosed.
The compact probe tests only judge 1 and one Check judge, so lenient judges 2 and 3 go undetected until Stage 6. Seeds written by the orchestrator may be too easy.
Judges do not see command results, so a variant that only turns a failing command green still needs 2 judge preferences. T1 may stall; this is in the Deferred table with a trigger.

UNKNOWN on a protected criterion blocks pruning but does not veto an improvement keep; only an explicit 'best' does. This trades order-noise vetoes for some regression risk, and strict mode is the remedy.
The new HALT(ERROR) may end runs on flaky infrastructure after two all-ERROR rounds, and the judge-3 trigger may spend one extra call when two judges tie a non-shorter variant.
In plain-chat mode the Verifier and Screen still run in the writer's context. The relay is slow, and printed records can be torn or misordered. None of this has been tested with a real human.
Fail-closed defaults will raise PARTIAL and HALT rates, which may read as a regression unless Output and README explain them.
'(nearly)' remains a judgment, and the checker's 0.9 ratio is arbitrary and advisory.
The majority pass at the Check and held-out stays despite leniency literature. The probe detects leniency but only strict mode corrects it, and the held-out gate stays majority.
Two rule definitions exist (the prose and rqgm_check.py) and can drift. Fixtures prove conformance only, and any meta-run rule change invalidates the Stage-1 answer key until it is re-adjudicated.
'optional' could be used to escape a failing gap. It is set at Setup, a later change is an amend, and Output labels it, but none of this is enforced in prose.
The budget start rule ('twice the costliest round') is a heuristic, and the first round is unconstrained.
Deleting the Stance section (strongest model, 'deletions welcome', one agent at a time) may change user-run behaviour without evidence either way.

Pilot validity: one model family; per-step orchestrator re-invocation differs from a real session; n = 1 per cell; T2 favours P by construction; sealed files have no technical boundary; about 700 calls at an unmeasured per-call cost need human approval; B's N and selection rule could bias the comparison (frozen in the manifest).
v3, like v2, was designed outside any run. Every claim is design-only until the pilot logs a run.

The judge-3 trigger becomes 'unless judges 1 and 2 prefer the same version' (judge 3's UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN ambiguity), so ties and UNKNOWN never skip judge 3. controller.rationale: Only a read-only checker is in scope, not a controller. Prose cannot guarantee anything mechanically. What it can make reliable are rules with four properties: (1) local, decidable from the inputs at hand at that step; (2) fail-closed, where the default is don't keep, don't pass, or [OPEN]; (3) few-branch; (4) visible in Output, so a human can audit them. v3 rewrites every safety rule into that form and keeps it in SKILL and INITIATOR. Rules that need cross-record bookkeeping cannot be carried by prose, so v3 either reduces them to record-derived forms or leaves them to the checker, which recomputes and never decides: per-call idempotency keys become a round-atomic resume; a per-call token ledger becomes rounds and time counted from records, with tokens nullable; hashes are computed only by the checker's hash command. Reservations, exactly-once and locks are rejected. The checker exists for two reasons. First, the orchestrator LLM is the least-audited actor, and the v2 dry-runs found the keep arithmetic ambiguous; making every decision recomputable from verbatim logged verdicts turns 'trust the orchestrator' into 'audit the orchestrator'. Second, the pilot needs a zero-model-call fault suite and a shadow audit. It is stdlib, read-only and optional, so the skill stays one product and there is no mode switch. The peer's owning controller (C01-C17, admission, reservation, hash-chained envelope, lock, fsync commit) solves concurrency and exactly-once problems a serial single-orchestrator prose loop does not have. It would also make a code-free host second-class.

cli_ops.name: audit MEMORY [--done DONE.json] [--target DIR] [--pending ROUND.json]
cli_ops.behavior: Read-only replay of archive.jsonl. A torn last line (unparsable or missing its newline) is reported as torn_tail and excluded. An interior unparsable line is an INTEGRITY error: exit 2, and nothing after it is audited. The checker recomputes state (best version id, rung, probe mode, stall count, rounds and minutes used, tokens or null, open required gaps, first held-out result, amends, due step round|check|boundary|stop|halt:REASON, status ACTIVE|PARTIAL|COMPLETE). For each logged decision it computes the decision the prose requires. It prints JSON {ok, state, violations:[{code, record_index, detail}], unauditable:[{rule, missing_field}], warnings:[...]}. Exit 0 = no violations, 1 = violations, 2 = integrity. A missing field makes a rule unauditable, never violated, so prose-mode archives degrade gracefully. --done hashes the current DONE file against the DONE text logged in setup. --target hashes check files against setup.check_hashes if present. --pending audits a not-yet-logged round as if appended and prints the keep it requires. The checker never writes any file.

cli_ops.name: selftest
cli_ops.behavior: Runs the bundled fixtures (tests/checker/fixtures/*.jsonl against expected.json). It passes only if each negative fixture yields exactly its expected violation codes (no extras) and each positive conformance fixture yields none. It uses no model calls, no network and no clock (fixture timestamps are data).

cli_ops.name: hash FILE... [--lf]
cli_ops.behavior: Prints the SHA-256 of each file (--lf normalizes CRLF to LF first), so that any hash appearing in MEMORY comes from a command, never from a model. It is optional at Setup for check files; prose mode never requires hashes.

controller.decision_policy: The checker encodes the prose exactly and only recomputes. RESULT: a judge value is A|B|tie, or UNKNOWN, or ERROR. Slot 1's two orders map to one preference if they agree, else UNKNOWN. An ERROR may be retried once; a second ERROR drops the variant with no ledger entry. 'Completed' means a verdict other than UNKNOWN or ERROR. GATES run in this order: apply ok, commands run in a copy (ERROR on a timeout or a tracked-file change), verifier (a contradicted claim is stripped; not-found becomes [OPEN]), then screen pass. A variant failing any gate is not judged. JUDGE: in normal mode, if slot 1 prefers best with confidence high, or rates a protected criterion worse, the variant is dropped. Otherwise slot 2 is required, and slot 3 is required unless slots 1 and 2 are completed with the same overall value. In strict mode, 3 slots are required and there is no early drop. KEEP-IMPROVE requires: prefer-variant count >= 2 (strict: 3); prefer-best count = 0; no slot rates a protected criterion worse (protected = guardrails, must-not-change constraints, and criteria the round's best passed at its last check); no protected command worse; all gates passed. KEEP-PRUNE requires: variant words < best words; completed slots >= 2 (strict: 3); no UNKNOWN or ERROR; no slot prefers best; no criterion rated worse; all gates passed. SELECT at most one per round: most prefer-variant, then fewer words, then earlier in the list. version.parent must equal round.best, which must equal the previous kept version. STALL = the count of consecutive rounds with kept=null since the last keep or escalation. A Check is due at stall = 3 or on a DONE claim. A check on a version that already has a failed check is a violation until the version changes. Check values: a command criterion from the command, a source criterion from the Verifier (unknown = unchecked), a judges criterion by majority of 3 (pass needs >= 2 pass). All pass leads to the boundary; below the final rung, the next round requires a human rung record plus a new probe, and the stall count resets. HALT(STALL) is valid only with stall >= 3 and a failing check. BUDGET: no round with n > budget.rounds or elapsed > budget.minutes; exit BUDGET requires a check on the current best after the last round. STOP: an open substrate with required = true forces exit OPEN. Held-out attempt 2 is valid only on a version different from attempt 1 that has an all-pass check; otherwise the exit must be OVERFIT. STATUS COMPLETE requires rung = final, the last check all-pass on best, a held-out pass on best, and no required open substrate; otherwise PARTIAL. An exit record whose status differs from the recomputed one is a FALSE_COMPLETE or MISLABEL violation. OSCILLATION (advisory): a kept diff whose whitespace-normalized 'new' has difflib ratio >= 0.9 to an earlier kept diff's 'old' in the same section, without an exit OSCILLATION, is a warning (the prose word '(nearly)' stays a human-visible judgment). DONE DRIFT: the current DONE hash differs from setup's DONE hash with no amend between is a violation; an amend touching a criterion that had failed before it is a warning, 'amended after failure'.

PRE-REGISTERED
Primary outcome: false completion (exit COMPLETE while the scorer finds a required failure), then oracle pass of required checks on the emitted artifact. Under f1, V treats the ERROR as a tie or rejection or re-samples it, while P retries once and drops without a ledger entry. Decision rule: the prose-first bet survives only if P shows zero false completions, zero P01-P16 violations and zero journal mismatches. Whether the v3 prose executes end to end in this host within the caps. On these two cases, P's oracle result and cost versus S and V at matched caps. Whether a prose-only orchestrator made invalid keeps, re-rolled checks, false completions or misrecorded verdicts. How the handled faults behaved. Judge leniency on seeded defects at tiny n.

WHAT IT CANNOT CONCLUDE
General superiority or the effect of any single change (n=1 per arm, no repeats). Cross-family independence (all roles run on one family; the 2 GPT uploads are a spot check). Real-human plain-chat usability (the harness relay is a proxy). Behaviour at E3. Crash safety beyond f4. That the checker's rules are the right rules (conformance is not correctness). Anything about controller enforcement, since no controller arm runs.

risks: The prose-first bet may simply be false. LLM orchestrators may misapply the 5-branch keep rule and the new UNKNOWN/ERROR classes; v2's text dry-runs alone found 18 ambiguities. The pilot's audit and journal comparison is the falsification test, and any observed violation must move that rule to checker-mandatory for shell hosts.

The audit checks internal consistency, not truth. The orchestrator writes MEMORY, so a misreported verdict passes. Only the pilot harness journal can measure records honesty; in user runs it stays unaudited.

Zero headroom. SKILL is at 997/1000, so every fix the pilot finds must displace a rule. The shortfall the register predicted was closed by compression, including about 22 tokens of formatting (bullets inline, separators changed to commas) that the str.split convention counts. That is disclosed, not hidden.

Probe cost. About 12 calls per rung (identity in both orders x 3 judges, seeded pairwise x 3, seeded Check x 3), rerun at each escalation. In a 30-45-call budget it consumes a quarter or more of the run, and may make v3 look worse than v2 on completion while better on false completion.

The seeded defect is written by the orchestrator, which has seen the generator's rationale. It may seed obvious defects, making the probe too easy and giving false confidence; no difficulty rule fits in the word budget.

Plain-chat mode keeps only the judges out of the writer's context. The Verifier and Screen then run in the writer's context, and the human relay and printed records are slow and error-prone (torn or misordered JSON). This is untested with a real human.
Fail-closed defaults will raise PARTIAL and HALT(STALL) rates. Users may read this as regression unless Output and README explain it.
'(nearly) restores' remains a judgment in prose; the checker's 0.9 ratio is arbitrary and advisory.
Majority pass at the Check and held-out stays despite leniency literature (a true-negative rate under 25%). The seeded probe detects leniency but does not correct a lenient majority.
Two definitions of the rules exist: the prose and rqgm_check.py. They can drift, and fixtures only prove conformance to the fixtures.
The 'optional' marking could be used to escape a failing gap. Mitigation: optional is set at Setup, any later change is an amend, and Output lists it; this is still unenforced in prose.
v3, like v2, is being designed outside any loop run. It must be labelled 'design review' until the pilot logs a run, and every claim above is design-only until then.

Pilot validity: all roles on one family; per-run caps unknown until prep; one run per arm; the harness relay is itself new code that could bias V against P if its prompt adapter treats v2's untyped DONE differently. The type mapping must be frozen and applied identically.

controller.rationale: In v2, one unaudited LLM runs a decision table with more than 12 branches: early drop, the judge-3 trigger, strict 3/3, the pruning keep, the protected veto, tie-breaks, stall, budget, oscillation, held-out retry. It also tracks keys, versions and spend, and resumes after crashes. This orchestrator is also the only actor that sees the generator's rationale. Two LLM dry-runs of the spec found 10, then 8, ambiguities in exactly these branches, and each fix round surfaced new ones (measured on spec text). The v1-era runs lost work on resume and logged apply errors as merit losses. A scratch prototype of the v3 panel rule also exposed one more v2 gap: two tying judges could prune with no third judge. Code gives each rule one definition. It makes every decision replayable and checkable offline. It lets hash and exit-code evidence be computed by a tool instead of asserted by an LLM, and it frees about 200 SKILL words. Limits, per the peer: code validates protocol, not truth. A wrong policy becomes reliably wrong. The controller is cooperative, not a sandbox. The bet stays design-only until validation Stages 1 and 3 measure how often prose orchestrators misapply the policy.

cli_ops.name: init
cli_ops.behavior: init --run DIR --workspace DIR --target PATH[,PATH] --done DONE.json --budget BUDGET.json --evaluators EVAL.json --heldout-sha256 HEX --spare-sha256 HEX --spec PATH [--human-channel tty|relay] [--from-request REQ.json | --from-prose ARCHIVE]. Refuses if DIR already holds an archive (use resume). Validates DONE v3: unique ids; kind in cmd|verify|judge; cmd needs argv and timeout_s; required is a bool; final_rung in E1..E3; frozen and check_inputs globs. Snapshots the workspace (TARGET, frozen and check-input files) into blobs. Hashes DONE, the spec file and GROUNDING. Appends RunInitialized and VersionAccepted(v0, verified:false). Prints {ok, run_id, next:{action:'seed'}}. Exit 0; 1 if refused; 2 for usage or integrity errors.

cli_ops.name: seed
cli_ops.behavior: seed --run DIR --file PATH --criterion ID. Stores a defective copy of best that breaks criterion ID; it must differ from best. Appends ProbeSeeded. Required before the probe at init and at each escalation. The prose rule says the human or orchestrator writes it, never a generator key.

cli_ops.name: next
cli_ops.behavior: next --run DIR. Idempotent. If an admitted call is still outstanding, returns the same envelope without a new reservation. Otherwise computes the next required step from the policy, admits it atomically (CallAdmitted with a reservation) and prints one of: {action:'call', key, role, persona, inputs:{name:path}, output_schema, reserve:{calls,tokens}}; {action:'run-check', key}; {action:'human', ask, options}; {action:'seed'}; {action:'halted', reason, report}; {action:'complete', report}. Judge envelopes hold only A and B files, and the A/B-to-variant mapping stays in controller state. Admission denial routes to Check or HALT(BUDGET) (policy rule 11). Hands out one call at a time.

cli_ops.name: record
cli_ops.behavior: record --run DIR --key KEY --result FILE --model NAME [--tokens N|null] [--seconds S]. The file is the role's JSON, unedited. Validates it against the key's role schema (generator_v1, verifier_v1, screen_v1, judge_v1, checkjudge_v1, gap_v1); a schema failure is stored as AttemptErrored(unparsable). Binds the result to the key's candidate, parent and rubric hashes. Same key and attempt with an identical sha is a no-op receipt; a different sha gives IDENTITY_CONFLICT (exit 1). A closed round or old parent gives STALE, and attempt 1 after attempt 2 gives LATE; both are stored, not counted. Generator results run APPLY, OUT_OF_SECTION, FROZEN and DUPLICATE and append CandidateProposed or CandidateRejected. Judge A/B verdicts are mapped to variant/best. Then runs advance(): the pure policy appends any decision (CandidateRejected, Dropped, Accepted, RoundClosed, CheckClosed, Halted) with the durable-blob-first commit order and materializes TARGET. Prints {ok, receipt, decisions}.

cli_ops.name: error
cli_ops.behavior: error --run DIR --key KEY --reason timeout|refusal|crash|unknown [--tokens N|null] [--seconds S]. Appends AttemptErrored. Attempt 2 becomes eligible at the next call to next if the slot has had fewer than 2 attempts. Otherwise the slot is final ERROR and advance() applies: DROP, forced REJECT, or HALT(ERROR) for a cmd check. Null usage keeps its reservation as spent.

cli_ops.name: run-check
cli_ops.behavior: run-check --run DIR --key KEY. The key names a candidate and a cmd criterion. Builds a temp dir from the init workspace snapshot, overlays the candidate's TARGET files, restores every frozen and check_inputs path from the snapshot (so generator-added tests and config are absent), and runs the frozen argv (shlex.split, no shell) with timeout_s. Appends CheckRecorded: exit 0 is PASS; nonzero is FAIL; timeout, a missing executable or any tracked file changed by the run is ERROR. Records stdout/stderr sha and seconds, then deletes the temp dir. This is the only op that can produce cmd results.

cli_ops.name: human
cli_ops.behavior: human --run DIR --ask escalate|stop|pick|heldout|close-gap|waive-gap|amend|approve-reframe|reject-reframe|receipt --by NAME [--value X] [--file F]. Requires an interactive TTY on stdin when human_channel=tty, else REFUSED_NOT_TTY. The Bash tool has no TTY, so the human types it in their own terminal. Appends HumanDecision{channel} plus the effect: RungAdvanced (E3 needs a prior Amended adding a criterion); Completed(PARTIAL); VersionAccepted(human_pick); HeldoutRecorded (criterion IDs PASS/FAIL only, attempt immutable); GapClosed (a factual gap needs --file evidence and triggers one Verifier call first); Amended (waive-gap, DONE/BUDGET change, with after_result); ReceiptRecorded.

cli_ops.name: resume
cli_ops.behavior: resume --run DIR [--break-lock] [--accept-policy VERSION]. Validates segments, the hash chain and blob references. A torn last line is copied to torn/<seq>.bin, and a SegmentStarted in archive.<k+1>.jsonl links the last valid hash. Interior corruption, or an accepted blob that is missing, gives HALT(ERROR:integrity). A policy_version mismatch is refused unless --accept-policy, which records a RunResumed boundary. An admitted call without a result gives CompletionUnknown: the liability is kept and attempt 2 is issued by next. If the TARGET hash is not best: a known version is re-materialized; an unknown hash (hand edit) sets human-pending target_drift. A stale lock is removed only with --break-lock after the user confirms no writer is live.

cli_ops.name: status
cli_ops.behavior: status --run DIR. Read-only. Prints phase, rung, best id and sha, round, stall, error_rounds, strict mode, budget {known, reserved, unknown_count, remaining}, open gaps, pending human asks, policy parameters and enforcement:'code'.

cli_ops.name: report
cli_ops.behavior: report --run DIR [--md PATH] [--envelope PATH]. Prints the Output: status COMPLETE|PARTIAL|HALTED(reason); best sha and paths; rung reached vs final; each criterion as PASS, FAIL, UNKNOWN or unchecked with how it was decided (cmd, verifier, judge-majority with the models' families, held-out) and the done_sha it was decided under; the first held-out outcome; amendments; gaps with class and owner; counts computed from events (proposed, kept, pruned, rejected by code, dropped); spend {calls, tokens_known, unknown_count, seconds}; human_channel; a correlated-source note when every judge shares the generator's family; one next action. --envelope writes the substrate result envelope.

cli_ops.name: replay
cli_ops.behavior: replay --archive FILE --done DONE.json [--policy rqgm-p3.0]. Read-only shadow replay and lint of a prose-mode archive (INITIATOR schema). Re-derives every keep, drop, stall, Check and halt from the recorded verdicts. Reports the first divergent decision, with a policy-parameter divergence (for example the '(nearly)' test) separated from an orchestrator error. Lists missing fields that make the archive unreplayable. Never writes and never splices later outputs.

controller.decision_policy:
Policy P3 (policy_version rqgm-p3.0). PROSE_MODE.md states the same rules in prose. Parameters are constants that status prints: 1 retry per slot; words = whitespace tokens over the TARGET files; oscillation = normalized (lowercased, whitespace-split) token edit distance <= max(5, ceil(0.02 x the longer version)); round_min = 1 + 2 x (2 + judges_min) calls (11 normal, 13 strict); final_reserve = 1 Verifier + 3 check-judges; probe = 4 calls.
(1) ROUND OPEN only if status is ACTIVE, rounds < max_rounds, time < deadline, and admission covers round_min + final_reserve. Otherwise Check best (unless a cached Check exists for this best, done_sha and rubric_sha) and go to Stop. If even the reserve cannot be admitted: HALT(BUDGET), reporting the last Check's labels. Parent p = best at open, frozen for the round.
(2) GENERATOR: one call returns up to 2 variants as exact-anchor edits {path, old, new}, each with a declared section (path#heading, or path for non-Markdown), a criterion and a hypothesis, plus claims_done.
(3) PER VARIANT, in order. (a) APPLY: every old anchor occurs exactly once in p, else ERROR. An anchor outside the declared section: REJECT(OUT_OF_SECTION). A frozen or check-input path: REJECT(FROZEN). A normalized diff identical to one rejected at this rung: REJECT(DUPLICATE). (b) CMD: run-check every cmd criterion. ERROR twice: DROP(ERROR). FAIL where p passes: REJECT(REGRESSION). A FAIL where p also fails is allowed. (c) VERIFY: one Verifier call. Any contradicted claim, or a not-found claim not inside [OPEN: ...], triggers one generator revision (new id, same parent, same proposal position); a failing revision is REJECT(VERIFY). (d) SCREEN: reject codes give REJECT(SCREEN:codes). needs-human also opens a NEEDS_HUMAN gap now, without pausing.
(4) PANEL: slot1 = judge 1 in AB and BA order. A/B is mapped to variant/best by the key; the judge never knows which is best. If both orders agree, slot1 takes that verdict; otherwise UNKNOWN, overall and per criterion. Protected = guardrail and must-not-change criteria, plus criteria p passed at the last Check or last cmd run. Normal mode: if slot1 prefers best in both orders with high confidence, or prefers best on a protected criterion, REJECT(EARLY). Otherwise slot2 (BA). slot3 (AB) runs if strict, if slot1 and slot2 differ overall, if slot1 is UNKNOWN, or if both tie and the variant has fewer words than p. Strict mode runs all 3 slots with no early drop.
(5) DECISION over completed slots. Any slot preferring best overall or on a protected criterion: REJECT(OBJECTION), with objections counted for the ledger. support = slots preferring the variant. KEEP if support >= 2 (strict: 3). PRUNE if the variant has fewer words than p, all 3 slots completed, every overall verdict is variant or tie, and no per-criterion verdict is best or UNKNOWN. Otherwise REJECT(NO_MAJORITY). A slot still ERROR after its retry: REJECT if the completed slots already force it, else DROP(ERROR). UNKNOWN never counts as support, tie, pass or non-regression. Confidence is used only for the early drop.
(6) SELECT at most one per round: most support, then fewer words, then proposal order. CandidateAccepted is appended only after its blob is durable; TARGET is then materialized (tmp then os.replace) and its hash checked. If the new best is within the oscillation distance of any earlier accepted version other than p: HALT(OSCILLATION). The human picks a version id, it becomes best, and the run resumes.
(7) STALL: a kept variant sets stall = 0. Otherwise, if any variant ended in a merit REJECT, stall + 1. Otherwise (every variant was DROPped) error_rounds + 1 and stall is unchanged. 2 consecutive error rounds: HALT(ERROR).
(8) CHECK when stall = 3 or claims_done is set. If the last Check failed on the same best, done_sha and rubric_sha, reuse it with zero calls. Otherwise check every criterion every time: cmd via run-check; all verify criteria in one Verifier call, PASS only with a locator; judge criteria by 3 fresh check-judges, PASS if at least 2 say PASS (strict: 3). UNKNOWN and ERROR are not PASS. All required PASS: go to Boundary. Else, if stalled: one generator tagging call (RETRIEVE or REFRAME per failing criterion, recorded as gaps), then HALT(STALL). Else continue.
(9) BOUNDARY: if rung < final, the human escalates or stops. Escalate appends RungAdvanced with a new rubric_sha (E3 requires a prior Amended that adds a criterion), re-runs the probe, sets stall = 0, counts only this rung's ledger, and voids earlier passes. Stop appends Completed(PARTIAL).
(10) STOP: a required open gap gives HALT(OPEN). Otherwise the human enters held-out attempt 1 (criterion IDs only). All required PASS: Completed(COMPLETE). Otherwise the first outcome is recorded as exposed and rounds resume focused on the failing IDs. The spare set is requested only after a Check passes on a changed best. If best is unchanged when the rounds stall: HALT(STALL). A spare fail gives HALT(OVERFIT).
(11) BUDGET: each call is admitted with a reservation (1 call, reserve_tokens) only if known + reserved + request <= cap - final_reserve; Check and probe calls may draw on the reserve. Null usage keeps its reservation as spent. Downtime counts against the wall deadline. A clock earlier than the last event gives HALT(ERROR).
(12) ATTEMPTS: at most 2 per slot. A result for a closed round or an old parent is stored as STALE, and a result for attempt 1 after attempt 2 was admitted is stored as LATE; neither is counted. The same key and attempt with a different payload gives IDENTITY_CONFLICT.
(13) PROBE (at init and at each escalation; needs a seed): the identity pair (1 call) must tie overall; the seeded pair, in both orders, must prefer best on the seeded criterion; one check-judge must FAIL the seed on that criterion. Any miss or UNKNOWN switches on strict mode and notifies the human; no judge is replaced.

invariants.rule: Only a complete required gate set permits a keep or a Check pass; ERROR and UNKNOWN never satisfy a gate
invariants.negative_test: Record screen ERROR twice for r2.a. advance gives DROP(ERROR): no CandidateAccepted, stall unchanged

invariants.rule: Every result is bound to its key's candidate hash, round-parent hash and rubric hash
invariants.negative_test: Open r3 on parent p2, then record a judge result against an r2 envelope minted for p1. The result is stored as STALE, best is unchanged and it is not counted

invariants.rule: One (key, attempt) identifies one payload
invariants.negative_test: Record r2.a.judge2.BA#1 as variant, then the same key and attempt as best. The second gives IDENTITY_CONFLICT (exit 1), and the tally counts only the first

invariants.rule: Recorded calls are never re-issued
invariants.negative_test: Archive with judge1 AB and BA recorded for r2.a and no decision. After resume, next returns the judge2 envelope, not judge1

invariants.rule: Admission never exceeds cap minus final reserve, counting outstanding reservations
invariants.negative_test: max_calls 100, final reserve 4: reserve 60, then request 50; and in the other order 50, then 60. The second request is denied both ways, and known + reserved stays <= 96

invariants.rule: Unknown usage stays a liability, never zero
invariants.negative_test: Admit a 20000-token call, then record --tokens null. Remaining tokens drop by 20000 and the report shows unknown_count = 1

invariants.rule: An acceptance never references missing bytes
invariants.negative_test: Delete the blob named by a CandidateAccepted. resume gives HALT(ERROR:integrity), exit 2

invariants.rule: COMPLETE requires every required criterion to PASS at the final rung, plus a held-out pass
invariants.negative_test: All required criteria PASS at E1 with final rung E2, then human stop: status is PARTIAL. An injected Completed(COMPLETE) is flagged as an integrity error on replay

invariants.rule: Objective, rung, pick, gap-closure and held-out entries come only through the human op
invariants.negative_test: A generator result carrying an 'amend' field gives SCHEMA_REJECT. Under channel=tty, human --ask amend with non-TTY stdin gives REFUSED_NOT_TTY

invariants.rule: Roles cannot self-certify
invariants.negative_test: record a cmd-kind check result: REFUSED, because only run-check writes cmd results. A verifier_v1 payload on a judge key: ROLE_MISMATCH

invariants.rule: A DONE or rubric change voids earlier passes
invariants.negative_test: c3 passes a Check at E1, then the run escalates to E2. The report lists c3 as unchecked at E2 until a new Check

invariants.rule: At most one acceptance per round
invariants.negative_test: After r4.a is accepted, an injected CandidateAccepted for r4.b is rejected as ROUND_CLOSED

invariants.rule: The first held-out outcome is immutable and always reported
invariants.negative_test: Attempt 1 FAILs c2 and the spare set PASSes. The report says c2 failed on the first attempt and passed spares after revision, never an unqualified pass. Re-entering attempt 1 gives IDENTITY_CONFLICT

invariants.rule: A torn tail cannot change best
invariants.negative_test: Truncate the CandidateAccepted line mid-JSON. On resume, best is the previous version, the bytes are saved to torn/<seq>.bin, and archive.1.jsonl starts by linking the last valid hash

invariants.rule: Only one writer at a time
invariants.negative_test: With a lock file held by a live pid, record gives LOCKED (exit 2). The lock is removed only by resume --break-lock

invariants.rule: A retry never erases the failed attempt or its liability
invariants.negative_test: error r2.a.judge2#1 --reason timeout --tokens null, then record #2. The report shows both attempts and 1 unknown-usage liability

invariants.rule: An initially failing artifact can still improve
invariants.negative_test: v0 fails c1 (cmd) and c2. A variant fixes only c1 and judges prefer it 2/2. Result: KEEP; c2 still failing does not block it

invariants.rule: UNKNOWN is never support, a tie or non-regression
invariants.negative_test: Judge 1 gives AB = variant and BA = best, so UNKNOWN. Judges 2 and 3 tie on a shorter variant. Result: REJECT(NO_MAJORITY), not PRUNE

invariants.rule: Pruning needs a completed 3-judge panel
invariants.negative_test: Shorter variant, judges 1 and 2 tie: next returns judge3, not a keep. If judge3 then ERRORs twice: DROP(ERROR), not PRUNE

invariants.rule: Frozen check inputs cannot be changed or bypassed
invariants.negative_test: (a) A variant edits test_public.py: REJECT(FROZEN). (b) A cmd that rewrites a tracked file: ERROR, not PASS. (c) A conftest.py added by the variant is absent from the check workspace

invariants.rule: A failed Check or held-out result stands until best changes
invariants.negative_test: A Check FAILs c2 on v4, then claims_done arrives with no keep: the stored result is returned with zero new calls. After a held-out fail with best still v4, the rounds stall: HALT(STALL), and the spare set is never requested

invariants.rule: Stall counts merit outcomes only
invariants.negative_test: A round where both variants are DROP(ERROR): stall unchanged, error_rounds = 1; a second such round gives HALT(ERROR). A round with two REJECTs: stall + 1

invariants.rule: Oscillation halts deterministically
invariants.negative_test: Accept v5 within max(5, 2%) normalized tokens of v3 (v5's parent is v4): HALT(OSCILLATION), and next returns a human pick. human --ask pick v5 returns the run to ACTIVE

invariants.rule: Out-of-section edits are rejected mechanically
invariants.negative_test: A variant declares SKILL.md#Stop but one anchor lies under '## Setup': REJECT(OUT_OF_SECTION)

out_of_scope: Distributed brokers, leases, fencing tokens, compare-and-swap, outboxes, sharding, databases (RUNTIME-ONLY: distributed-runtime, epoch-drain)
Concurrent or parallel dispatch (next hands out one call at a time) and atomic reservation across concurrent calls
Model invocation, web retrieval, or any command other than DONE's frozen argv via run-check
Authentication, sandboxing and held-out secrecy (the human keeps the prompts outside; the controller stores only hashes). The controller is cooperative, not a security boundary
Scientific knowledge graph, dependency inference, source supersession beyond citation status; the typed network and action taxonomy (science-state-model)
Evaluator replacement inside a run, global multi-project budgets, 100-200-agent scheduling
Bundled formal or numeric verifiers (Lean, sympy adapters); a cmd criterion may call them
Matched-budget baseline arms or repeated seeds inside a run (per-run-study-apparatus; validation only)
record_dispatch op, PolicySelected event, permission scopes, evaluation-set IDs beyond primary and spare, persisted monotonic clock
controller.degraded_mode: Prose mode is PROSE_MODE.md, byte-identical to INITIATOR's THE LOOP. The orchestrator LLM executes the same policy P3 serially, writing the INITIATOR archive schema with the header {"t":"run","loop":"v3","enforcement":"prose"}. Reduced forms: round-atomic resume replaces per-call keys (rerun any round without variant records; set a torn line aside); usage is logged per round, with null for unknown; LLMs never write hashes (only a command does, if a shell exists); the oscillation test is the prose '(nearly)'; human decisions are taken from chat. Output must say 'enforcement: prose' and claim no atomic persistence, hard budget or crash-safe resume. Switching modes is never silent. Code to prose: HALT, run `report --envelope handoff.json`, then start a new prose run with a 'continues: <run_id>' header and the remaining (not original) budget, without inheriting certification. Prose to code: run `replay` to lint the prose archive, then `init --from-prose` it as a new run. Audit: `rqgmctl.py replay` can lint a finished prose archive and name the first decision the controller would have made differently. This is an audit, not enforcement.

plan.substrate_interface:
Implement now only the envelope, no adapter: at most 80 lines in rqgmctl.py plus 2 round-trip tests; label design-only.

(1) Substrate to RQGM. `init --from-request REQ.json` accepts: request_id; target {ref, sha256}; parent_snapshot_id; objective {done_sha256, rubric_version}; evidence_refs[], which become hashed GROUNDING; capabilities[], recorded only, since the controller grants none; budget_allocation {id, caps}, which become the run's caps, so the parent owns the budget and RQGM only reserves inside it, and usage is reported once for the parent to aggregate; output_contract; stop {final_rung, deadline}.

(2) RQGM to substrate. `report --envelope OUT.json` emits: request_id; candidate {sha256, manifest, diff_from_v0}; snapshot_id; parent_sha256; policy_version; check versions (cmd argv plus frozen-input hashes); per-criterion {verdict, how decided, done_sha256}; provenance (model per role call); cost {calls, tokens_known, unknown_count, seconds}; gaps[] with class and owner; status COMPLETE|PARTIAL|HALTED(reason); enforcement.

(3) Receipt. `human --ask receipt --file RECEIPT.json` records {accepted|rejected|stale, reason, committed_revision}. Local best is only a proposal until the receipt arrives (two-stage promotion). A stale receipt means the snapshot changed: start a new run from the committed revision, never a patch-up.

As a Development/Meta-Evaluator loop, RQGM freezes its judges and rubric for the run. A successor evaluator is the TARGET of a separate run, with successor-development evidence kept apart from untouched evaluation evidence, and the outer authority decides its promotion. The loop therefore never changes a judge and then certifies itself with it.

Defer: transport, authentication, leases, the shared knowledge graph, dependency invalidation from substrate revisions, and multi-job scheduling. They are not needed for one orchestrator, and the envelope isolates them so adding them later changes an adapter, not the policy.

plan.validation:
Run the stages in order and stop at the first that fails. Labels are never upgraded.

STAGE 0: the controller, with zero model calls.
- Implement rqgmctl.py and run test_invariants.py (C01-C24, one negative test each).
- Run test_faults.py, which is the peer's section 4.3 table: malformed verdict (including duplicate JSON keys); timeout on a fake clock; stale parent; a crash before, during and after the acceptance append (via RQGM_CRASH_AT); an external completion that was never recorded (becomes COMPLETION_UNKNOWN); reservations of 60 and 50 against a cap of 100, in both orders; null usage; a late result from an old attempt. Add one real subprocess-kill-and-restart test and report it separately.
- Run test_conformance.py on 5 fault-free traces: imperfect v0, incremental keep, valid prune, complete run, honest partial halt. A controller that rejects everything fails these.
- Pass means zero invalid acceptances, no duplicate acceptance, no lost recorded result, and no admission overspend.
- This concludes only that the implementation handled these enumerated faults under Python 3.13 on Windows/NTFS.

STAGE 1: measure the bet, outside the pilot budget.
- Freeze PROSE_MODE.md and 30 synthetic decision scenarios. Each scenario is an archive state plus new results, and asks for the next decision. They cover: ERROR vs tie, judge-1 order disagreement, strict mode, pruning, the protected veto, tie-break, ERROR rounds and stall, unchanged-best reuse, spare gating, the round-plus-Check budget, amendments, and resume.
- The expected answer is the controller's output after the human adjudicates every scenario against the prose. A disagreement fixes the text or the code, followed by a re-freeze, all before any scoring.
- Then 3 fresh Claude orchestrator contexts per scenario answer from PROSE_MODE.md alone (about 90 short Workflow subagent calls). One upload of the whole set to the GPT peer adds one cross-family context.
- Report the misapplication rate by scenario class.
- Pre-registered reading: at most 1 error in 30 per context means the controller is worth only crash, budget and attestation safety, and live C stays deferred. 3 or more in 30 means a live C arm gets priority.
- This concludes synthetic bookkeeping error rates for these models. It says nothing about live-run rates or artifact outcomes.

STAGE 2: the pilot, the peer's section 4.1 design unchanged, at most 198 calls.
- Arms: S (one tool-using agent with the same public checks and budget), V (frozen v2), P (v3 prose with an LLM orchestrator, enforcement: prose).
- Tasks: the sealed T1 and T2 fixtures, one run per arm and task.
- Caps per run: 30 model calls, 60k tokens, 60 tool calls, 15 minutes. 18 preparation calls go to disposable examples.
- Controls: serial roles, randomized arm order, memory reset between arms.
- One model fills every role, including the held-out judges. This is a correlated-source limitation that P's report must print.
- The manifest freezes a per-task criterion-kind map, given to V and P alike with no privileged checks:
  - T1: t1-public is cmd; t1-spec and t1-interface are verify; t1-clarity is judge.
  - T2: t2-numbers, t2-required, t2-claims and t2-unknowns are verify; t2-clarity is judge.
- Endpoint: the sealed score.py on each emitted artifact (hidden tests and answer key), plus false completion, per-criterion regressions, cost with nulls, and process coverage. V and P run the sealed held-out judges only as their own Stop step.
- Preparation must show P completes the probe (4 calls), one round (about 11-13) and a Check (4) within 30 calls. If not, change the task size before freezing, never the mechanisms.
- Expect one round per run, so V vs P mainly tests probe, verification and Check behaviour, not search.

STAGE 3: shadow replay, zero calls.
- Run `rqgmctl.py replay` on each P archive. Report the first divergent decision, separating policy-parameter divergences from orchestrator errors, and freeze the comparison there. Never splice later P outputs onto a controller continuation.
- An unreplayable P archive is itself a finding.

STAGE 4 (optional): live C.
- Only if Stage 0 passes and Stage 1 crosses its threshold: 4 arms x 2 tasks x 24 calls = 192. Report C vs P as a package-level enforcement comparison.

GPT peer (at most 3 uploads):
- A blind conformance review of PROSE_MODE.md against CONTROLLER.md before freezing (design-only).
- The Stage-1 scenario set (one measured context).
- A review of the pilot records (design-only).

What the validation cannot conclude:
- That v3 beats v2 or a single agent in general.
- Statistical significance (n = 1 per cell).
- That code enforcement improves artifacts (no live C unless Stage 4 runs).
- Crash safety beyond the enumerated faults.
- Judge independence across frontier model families.
- Anything about 100-200-agent scale.

risks: If the encoded policy is wrong, it becomes reliably wrong (peer). Mitigation: the human adjudicates the 30 scenarios and 5 fault-free traces against the prose before any scored run.

Two normative texts can drift: PROSE_MODE.md/INITIATOR and rqgmctl.py. test_docs pins the byte identity and the scenario-set sha, and any policy change bumps policy_version and forces re-adjudication.

The bet may fail. If Stage 1 finds at most 1/30 prose misapplications, about 1000 lines of controller buy only crash, budget and attestation safety, which no run has needed yet: no run reached HALT(BUDGET), and the only resume failure is v1-era.
Orchestration overhead: about 3 CLI calls per role call add orchestrator turns and tokens. Measure and report them; do not hide them.

The controller is cooperative only. An orchestrator can drop an unfavourable output before recording it, forge relayed human decisions, or edit files. The hash chain detects some edits and the relay channel is labelled unauthenticated, but it is not a sandbox.
run-check executes candidate code locally (T1) with only a timeout. Run it in a disposable workspace; it is not a security boundary.
INITIATOR is at 1297/1300 words, so any future prose rule needs a same-size cut. PROSE_MODE.md is the long pole of the paste-and-go path.

Budget: with round_min + final_reserve admission, a 30-call pilot run gets about one round, and strict mode (13-call rounds) can get none. V vs P then mostly tests probe, verification and Check behaviour, not search.
Seeded-defect quality is unvalidated. A trivial seed passes lenient judges; an overly subtle one forces strict mode every time and exhausts the budget.

The design-only parameters (oscillation max(5, 2%), whitespace-token words, 1 retry, round_min 11) can diverge from the prose's '(nearly)'. Replay must report policy-parameter divergences separately from orchestrator errors.
Windows durability: os.replace is atomic on one NTFS volume, but directories cannot be fsynced, so power-loss safety is not claimed.
Evidence base: every 'measured' failure motivating v3 comes from v1-era runs or spec dry-runs, and v2 never ran end-to-end. All v3 claims stay design-only until Stages 0-3 report.
Mode confusion: a skill host that misjudges whether Python is available may start in prose mode. The mode is recorded in MEMORY, printed by every report, and switching mid-run is forbidden.

controller.rationale: In scope only as measurement apparatus, not as an enforcer. The pilot must tell whether the prose orchestrator followed its own rules, which needs a deterministic, pre-registered reading of the prose. That reading also yields archive linting and record-derived reports for free (counts-from-records, archive-lint-script). It costs zero model calls and cannot change a run. The peer's full controller is deferred: admission/reservation, hash-chained segments, writer lock, COMPLETION_UNKNOWN, role authentication and a live C arm. No v2 or v3 run has shown the prose orchestrator misapplying a rule, and the pilot's external meter already bounds spend. Enforcement also alters scheduling and feedback, confounding any P-vs-C comparison. Pre-registered promotion rule: build the live enforcing arm only if shadow replay finds at least one VIOLATION that changed a keep, Check or halt decision in P.

cli_ops.name: apply
cli_ops.behavior: `rqgm_policy.py apply VARIANT.json BASE_DIR` → {ok, class: OK|ERROR, errors, words_before, words_after, diff_path}. Each `old` anchor must occur exactly once in its declared file, and edits outside the declared file are ERROR. Never judges merit, never writes TARGET; output goes to a content-addressed scratch dir (lifted from meta_tool.py).

cli_ops.name: decide
cli_ops.behavior: `decide ROUND.json` (stdin/stdout, pure). Input: {mode, protected_ids, best_words, variants:[{id, order, apply, screen, mech{cid}, verdicts[{slot, orders[], overall, conf, per_criterion, protected_worse}]}]}. Output: per variant {status: REJECTED|REJECTED_PROTECTED|DROP_ERROR|DROP_EARLY|NEEDS_SLOT(k)|ELIGIBLE_IMPROVE|ELIGIBLE_PRUNE|NOT_ELIGIBLE, support}, keep: id|null, stall_increment: 0|1, osc_similarity. Applies the decision_policy exactly.

cli_ops.name: check
cli_ops.behavior: `check CHECK.json` → per criterion {state: PASS|FAIL|UNCHECKED, by: command|judges|heldout, votes}, required_all_pass, failing_required[], reuse: true when (best_id, rung) equals the last Check's.

cli_ops.name: lint
cli_ops.behavior: `lint ARCHIVE.jsonl [--calllog CALLS.jsonl]` → {violations:[{seq, code}]} with codes SCHEMA, TORN_TAIL, DUP_SLOT, TWO_KEEPS, UNSUPPORTED_KEEP, ERROR_COUNTED, STALL_MISCOUNT, MISSED_CHECK, REROLL_CHECK, REROLL_HELDOUT, KEPT_TEXT_MISMATCH (needs the call log's input hashes), POST_HALT. Read-only: never modifies or truncates the file; a torn tail is reported, and state is computed from the valid prefix.

cli_ops.name: replay
cli_ops.behavior: `replay CALLS.jsonl DECISIONS.jsonl --mapping eval/manifest.json` → walks each decision point, recomputes it with decide/check from the harness's true role outputs, and compares it with the orchestrator's recorded decision. Returns {agreed_points, first_divergence: {seq, kind, expected, actual, class: VIOLATION|AMBIGUOUS}} and stops there: no splicing of later outputs.

cli_ops.name: report
cli_ops.behavior: `report ARCHIVE.jsonl [--calllog]` → the v3 Output block computed from records: status, per-criterion state and decider, first and later held-out results, probe mode and misses, amendments, rounds, wall seconds from ts, tokens = sum only if every call reports them, else null plus null_count.

records: Archive (written by the loop, per INITIATOR/schema.md; every record has ts): spec{version}; version{id,parent,change}; variant{round,id,section,hypothesis,screen,mech{cid:PASS|FAIL|ERROR},verdicts[{slot,model,overall:A|B|tie|UNKNOWN|ERROR,conf}],kept}; citation{claim,source,status:verified|contradicted|not-found}; probe{mode,misses}; check{rung,pass{cid:true|false|null}}; rung{name}; amend{what,why,by}; substrate{gap,owner,status}; heldout{attempt,pass}; halt{reason}

Harness call log (eval only; ground truth independent of what the orchestrator logs): call{seq,arm,task,run,round,role,slot,order,attempt,variant,input_sha256,output_sha256,output,model,tokens|null,seconds,status:OK|ERROR(reason)}
Harness decision log (V/P only): decision{seq,round,kind:dispatch|drop|keep|stall|check|boundary|stop|halt,value,orchestrator_output_sha256}
Tool outputs (derived, never appended to the archive): lint{violations}, replay{agreed_points,first_divergence}, report{status,criteria,probe,amendments,rounds,wall_s,tokens|null,null_count}
Pilot score (human-run sealed scorer): score{arm,task,run,scorer_sha256,criteria{cid:PASS|FAIL},claimed_status,false_completion}
controller.decision_policy: Pre-registered reading of the v3 prose. It is an audit reference, not enforcement. Slot k in {1,2,3} is the k-th EVALUATORS persona (cycled if only 2). After un-blinding, overall is in {variant, best, tie, UNKNOWN, ERROR}. (1) Admission, per variant in proposal order. Every anchor must apply exactly once in the declared file, else ERROR. Screen REJECT → REJECTED. Any criterion that best passes by command and the variant FAILs → REJECTED_PROTECTED, before any judge. An ERROR in apply, screen or a command → rerun once; a second ERROR → DROP_ERROR (not a loss, no ledger block). (2) Judging. Judge 1 runs both orders; if the orders differ in overall, judge 1 is UNKNOWN; its confidence is the lower of the two orders. Normal mode: judge 1 = best with conf=high, or any order marks a protected item worse → DROP_EARLY. Otherwise request slot 2. Request slot 3 unless j1 == j2 and neither is UNKNOWN. Strict mode: all 3 slots, no early drop. A slot with two ERRORs → DROP_ERROR. (3) Eligibility. Improvement: count(variant) >= 2 (strict: 3), count(best) = 0, no protected-worse. Pruning: words(variant) < words(best), every requested slot completed (>= 2; strict: 3), all overall in {variant, tie}, no per-criterion 'best', no UNKNOWN or ERROR. Confidence never adds weight. (4) Selection: at most one keep, by max count(variant), then fewer words, then earlier proposal. A kept variant sets stall := 0; otherwise stall += 1, including all-rejected and all-ERROR rounds. (5) Check. Request one when stall = 3, or on a DONE claim if (best_id, rung) differs from the last Check's; otherwise REUSE the last result. Command criteria: PASS or FAIL from the harness-run command; two ERRORs → UNCHECKED, never judged. Judged criteria: PASS iff at least 2 of 3 PASS (strict: 3 of 3); UNKNOWN and ERROR are not PASS. Only required criteria gate. Then: all required PASS → BOUNDARY (rung < final → HUMAN_PAUSE, else STOP); some required fail with stall >= 3 → HALT(STALL); else CONTINUE. A held-out FAIL counts as a failing result until best or rung changes. (6) Stop. An open substrate linked to a required criterion → HALT(OPEN); else HELDOUT attempt 1. All required PASS (majority; strict 3/3) → COMPLETE. An attempt-1 fail → CONTINUE on the failing IDs. Attempt 2 (spares) only after a new kept version and a passing Check; an attempt-2 fail → HALT(OVERFIT). Stopping below the final rung → PARTIAL. (7) Budget: rounds or wall time at the cap, or tokens only when every call reports them → HALT(BUDGET) at the next decision point. (8) Not decided by code: screen merit, Verifier status, seeding quality, oscillation. decide reports the maximum whitespace-normalized word-sequence similarity to earlier bests and flags >= 0.98 as OSC_FLAG. Disagreements there are AMBIGUOUS, not VIOLATION. Prose ambiguities found later enter the manifest as numbered amendments before replay results are inspected.

invariants.rule: UNKNOWN never supports a keep or counts as 'not worse'
invariants.negative_test: j1 orders disagree (UNKNOWN), j2=tie, j3=tie, variant 10 words shorter, no criterion worse → decide must return keep=null (pruning denied)

invariants.rule: ERROR is not a verdict or a loss
invariants.negative_test: j2 returns ERROR on both attempts → status DROP_ERROR (not NOT_ELIGIBLE/LOSE), ledger_block=false, stall_increment=1 when nothing else is kept

invariants.rule: Confidence only stops spending
invariants.negative_test: j1=best conf=med → NEEDS_SLOT(2), not DROP_EARLY; j1=variant conf=high with j2=best → no keep (confidence adds no vote)

invariants.rule: Judge-3 trigger treats UNKNOWN as matching nothing
invariants.negative_test: j1=variant, j2=UNKNOWN → NEEDS_SLOT(3); j1=UNKNOWN, j2=UNKNOWN → NEEDS_SLOT(3); j1=j2=variant → no slot 3 requested

invariants.rule: Strict mode: no early drop, and a keep needs 3/3
invariants.negative_test: strict, j1=best conf=high → NEEDS_SLOT(2); strict, 2 of 3 prefer the variant → keep=null

invariants.rule: One keep per round, chosen deterministically
invariants.negative_test: two eligible variants with equal support and equal words → the earlier proposal is kept; the other is ELIGIBLE but not kept

invariants.rule: Every round with nothing kept is a stall round
invariants.negative_test: both variants REJECTED or DROP_ERROR → stall_increment=1

invariants.rule: No Check re-roll on an unchanged best and rung
invariants.negative_test: DONE claim with (best_id, rung) equal to the last failed Check's → check.reuse=true, no judge requests; an archive with two check records for the same (best, rung) → lint REROLL_CHECK

invariants.rule: No held-out re-roll, and the first result is preserved
invariants.negative_test: heldout attempt 2 with no kept version after attempt 1 → lint REROLL_HELDOUT; report still shows attempt 1's FAIL when attempt 2 passes

invariants.rule: Optional criteria never gate
invariants.negative_test: all required PASS and an optional one FAILs → required_all_pass=true, next is BOUNDARY/STOP, not HALT(STALL)

invariants.rule: HALT(OPEN) only for gaps a required criterion needs
invariants.negative_test: the only open substrate is linked to an optional criterion → stop decision HELDOUT, not HALT(OPEN)

invariants.rule: Judges never stand in for an ERRORed command
invariants.negative_test: command c1 ERRORs twice and 3 judges mark c1 PASS → c1=UNCHECKED, required_all_pass=false

invariants.rule: A protected mechanical regression is rejected before judging
invariants.negative_test: best passes c1, variant FAILs c1 → REJECTED_PROTECTED, no judge slot requested

invariants.rule: Counts and costs come from records; missing usage is null
invariants.negative_test: archive with 5 variant rounds plus a note record claiming 3 → report.rounds=5; a call log with one null-token call → tokens=null, null_count=1 (never 0)

invariants.rule: A torn tail is reported, never repaired
invariants.negative_test: last line cut mid-JSON → lint TORN_TAIL, state from the valid prefix, file SHA-256 unchanged before and after lint

invariants.rule: At most one kept variant per round in any archive
invariants.negative_test: two variant records with kept:true in round 4 → lint TWO_KEEPS

invariants.rule: Replay stops at the first divergence and never splices
invariants.negative_test: trace where the orchestrator kept a pruning variant with j1=UNKNOWN → first_divergence {expected NO_KEEP, actual KEEP, class VIOLATION}; no later round evaluated

invariants.rule: The probe turns on strict mode on any miss
invariants.negative_test: 1 of 3 Check judges grades the seeded copy PASS on its named criterion → probe mode=strict; all FAIL, pairwise prefers best, identity ties → normal

invariants.rule: An apply failure is ERROR, never a rejection
invariants.negative_test: anchor found 0 or 2 times → class ERROR; decide never returns REJECTED or NOT_ELIGIBLE for it

invariants.rule: Fault-free conformance (guards against a reject-everything policy)
invariants.negative_test: hand-built valid trace (imperfect v0 → improvement keep → pruning keep → Check pass → E2 → Check pass → held-out pass) replays with 0 divergences and reports COMPLETE; the same trace cut before E2 reports PARTIAL

invariants.rule: An imperfect v0 does not block repair
invariants.negative_test: v0 fails c1 and c2; a variant fixes c1 (c2 still failing) and 2/2 judges prefer it → keep=variant

invariants.rule: Kept text is exactly the judged text
invariants.negative_test: the kept version's hash differs from the input hash its judge calls saw → lint KEPT_TEXT_MISMATCH
