controller.degraded_mode: The loop never depends on the tool. Without Python, runs follow SKILL.md or INITIATOR.md prose exactly as they do with it: the tool never enforces, so no mode label is needed and no mode can switch mid-run. The only runtime disclosure is the INITIATOR single-context label. Anyone with Python can run lint and report on an archive after the fact. In the pilot, if the tool crashes on a trace, that trace's replay is recorded as ERROR and its outcomes are still scored. No claim of atomic persistence, hard budget enforcement or crash-safe recovery is made in any mode.

plan.substrate_interface: Defer. RQGM has not been shown to add value over a single agent (S) or best-of-N with the same checks (B) at matched budget, and adapting it to the peer's Scientific Loop substrate would integrate an unvalidated component. Two forward-compatible commitments cost nothing now. (1) Every archive record carries ts, and the harness call log carries input/output SHA-256, model, and usage or null. The peer's RQGM-to-substrate result message (candidate hash, parent hash, check versions, scoped outcomes, known/unknown cost, gaps, status) can therefore be derived later from records without rerunning anything. (2) A local COMPLETE is never an outer commit: any future adapter submits a proposal, and the outer authority decides and revalidates. Revisit only if P or V beats both S and B on the primary endpoint at equal ceilings. Then implement the peer's three messages (request, result, receipt) as an adapter over `rqgm_policy.py report`, outside the loop prose, with the evaluator frozen per run and successor evidence kept separate from untouched evaluation evidence.

plan.validation:
Stage 0 (0 model calls):
(a) tools/test_rqgm_policy.py runs P01-P22, including the P20 conformance trace, so that 'passes the faults' cannot mean 'rejects everything'.
(b) eval/test_harness.py runs fake-adapter faults: timeout, malformed JSON, late superseded result, ceiling hit mid-round, and a sealed-path scan of every capsule.
(c) Scorer sanity, run by the human because the scorer is sealed: score untouched v0, the sealed references and the existing decoys, and confirm the scorer separates them.
(d) Freeze eval/manifest.json and commit it before any scored call. It records hashes of V (SKILL/INITIATOR at 24663bd), P (v3 files), the S/B/role/orchestrator prompts, the prose-to-policy mapping with its ambiguities, the model id and the ceilings. It also scripts the human decisions: escalate to E2 when offered, never amend, never close an [OPEN], and at HALT(OSCILLATION) pick the newer best.

Stage 1 (at most 18 calls, disposable toy artifacts only): measure the cost of one complete V run. Set identical per-run ceilings (calls, Workflow-reported tokens, wall time) at 1.25x the smallest ceiling at which V reaches its held-out check; start the smoke at 80 calls. The only measured cost datum is ~60K tokens per agent call in the meta-run (4.52M/75), so the peer's 30-call/60K-token cap would fund about one call and is rejected.

Stage 2 (arms on T1, T2 and T3; T3 is written by the human after the freeze and shown to no design agent):
- S: one agent, one context, the same tools, public tests and corpus.
- B: best-of-N fresh single revisions, plus the same harness-run checks and one Verifier call per candidate; selection by public-check passes, then Verifier flags, then length. This is the fixed-verification arm: it tests whether checks plus selection alone explain any gain.
- V: frozen v2.
- P: v3.
V and P run in one Workflow harness. An orchestrator-decision call reads the spec text plus the archive and returns the next action. The script only dispatches fresh-context roles with the Roles capsules, applies diffs deterministically, runs requested commands in a scratch copy with time limits, meters usage and logs every call. It never corrects a protocol error. One run per arm per task: 12 runs, randomized order, memory reset, no cross-arm sharing. S and B also run at a 0.5x ceiling, giving a two-point cost curve.

Endpoints:
- Primary: the sealed scorer's pass on all required criteria of the final emitted artifact.
- False completion: an arm reports COMPLETE or all-pass, but the scorer finds a required failure.
- Secondary: regressions vs v0, justified abstention on T2's unknown field, cost including failed calls and null-token counts, and the in-run probe outcomes.
- Clarity: one blind GPT-peer upload per task, with arms anonymized and order randomized (3 of the few cross-family calls), labelled preference. The GPT peer is never an in-loop judge because of its latency.

Stage 3 (0 calls): shadow replay of the V and P call and decision logs through rqgm_policy.py gives the first divergence per run, classed VIOLATION or AMBIGUOUS by the frozen mapping, with no splicing after it.

Stage 4 (after all arm runs, so the sealed references never touch an arm; ~72 calls): judge calibration J. Per task: 4 human-seeded defects on the sealed reference, plus 1 identity and 1 rewording pair, judged with the arms' exact pairwise prompt (both orders) and Check prompt (3 judges). Measures: pairwise miss rate, absolute false-pass rate, order-reversal rate. Total is roughly 400-500 subagent calls; the smoke sets the exact figure, and the human approves spend before Stage 2.

Pre-registered decisions:
- Any P false completion, or P below S or B on the primary endpoint for any task → no 'improved' claim, README stays 'unvalidated', and the next step is diagnosis, not new rules.
- S or B at or above P on every task → report 'no advantage observed over simpler methods on these cases'.
- At least one VIOLATION in P that changed a keep, Check or halt decision → build the live enforcing arm C for a follow-up; none → the controller stays an auditor.
- J false-pass above 50% → Check passes on that task type are reported as unreliable, and a minority-veto Check becomes the next candidate, tested prospectively.

Can conclude: whether each frozen procedure runs within equal ceilings; per-case outcomes, false completions and costs; how often the prose orchestrator departs from its own pre-registered rules; judge miss rates on seeded defects for these artifacts and one model family.

Cannot conclude:
- General or statistically reliable superiority (1 run per cell, 3 small tasks, possible ceiling effects).
- The effect of any single v3 rule (V to P is a package).
- Cross-family judging effects: in-harness judges are one family.
- Behaviour in a real user session: the harness splits the orchestrator into per-decision calls.
- Anything about papers or large codebases.

Disclosures:
- I read the public T1/T2 DONE files, not sealed/.
- T2's optional unknown field was co-designed with the optional-[OPEN] rule that P adopts, so P's T2 status advantage is by construction. Only T3 is design-blind.
- Sealed files have no technical access boundary. A post-run scan of all call inputs for sealed filenames and 8-grams of the answer key voids any leaked run.

rejected.item: Producing or validating v3 by a recursive RQGM meta-run on its own spec (runs/2026-09-25-peer/tools/meta_tool.py)
rejected.why: Same-family judges preferring a spec shaped by same-family judges is a preference measurement: the Goodhart path the loop itself warns about (challenge.missing[4]). Such a run may polish wording but is labelled 'design review' and cannot replace the pilot.

rejected.item: Raising the SKILL (1000) or INITIATOR (1300) word caps
rejected.why: They are the release gate. v3 fits (995 and 1287, counted with wc -w on scratch drafts) by cutting inert slogans and moving the schema into a bundled schema.md.

rejected.item: Peer pilot ceilings (30 calls / 60K tokens per run, 198 calls total) and 'arm N = revised prose' without a fixed-verification arm
rejected.why: The only measured cost datum (~60K tokens per agent call) makes those ceilings infeasible for V to reach its held-out check. Ceilings come from the Stage-1 smoke. Arm B is added so that gains from checks plus selection are not credited to judging.

rejected.item: Dropping the rewording control from the probe (peer: paraphrase legitimately changes clarity criteria)
rejected.why: The confound is real, but a false trigger only makes strict mode more conservative. Keeping the control minimizes the V-to-P difference; the confound is documented in DESIGN row 3.

rejected.item: Evidence upgrades from the peer's reference-kernel contract tests, the 5/5 v2-validation judge agreement, 2512.08296's 17.2x, or 2607.27942's 'checkers ratify framing'
rejected.why: The kernel tests describe different software, 5/5 agreement is equally consistent with v2 being better, 17.2x comes from an arm with no voting, and 2607.27942's figures must come from extracted text (WebFetch reversed a statistic).

risks: The pilot is underpowered: 1 run per cell and 3 small tasks. It can expose false completion, crashes and protocol drift, but a null or mixed result is the likely outcome and must not be over-read either way.
Ceiling effect: T1/T2 are tiny (47-106-word artifacts), so S may pass everything. The honest result may be 'the loop costs more for the same outcome', which is a finding, not a failure of the pilot.

External validity: the Workflow engine forbids nested subagents, so the orchestrator is split into per-decision calls with harness-built capsules. This is not how a user runs the skill in one Claude Code session, and context-leak failures are not measured.
All in-harness judges come from one family, so the v3 cross-family rule is never exercised. Agreement among V/P judges is one correlated source.

Contamination: I read the public T1/T2 DONE files. T2's optional unknown field was co-designed with a rule P adopts. Sealed files sit in a readable local path with no technical boundary; only T3 is design-blind, and only if the human writes it after the freeze.

v3 costs more per run than v2 (seeding plus about 5 probe calls, more judge-3 runs from UNKNOWN, strict mode whenever the probe finds a miss). At equal ceilings P has fewer rounds, which may lower its outcomes even if every rule is correct.
An orchestrator-seeded defect may be trivial, so the probe passes vacuously. Judge calibration with human-seeded defects is the check, but it runs only after the arms.

Shadow replay is only as good as the frozen prose-to-policy mapping. Ambiguities discovered afterwards must be recorded as amendments before replay results are inspected, or replay becomes a tuning loop.

SKILL.md has 5 spare words and INITIATOR.md 13, so any post-pilot fix requires cuts. The bundled schema.md moves words rather than deleting them, and a host that copies only SKILL.md loses the field list.
Cost: roughly 400-500 subagent calls at an unmeasured per-call token cost. The smoke must price the pilot, and the human must approve spend before Stage 2.
Removing 'When CPU-bound, run one agent at a time' and 'deletions welcome' to fit the cap may slightly change user-run behaviour without evidence either way.
